sleeve_gate.sentence: No sleeve-level gate earns adoption: switching the sleeve off on trend 24%, vol 30%, drawdown 16% of the decision grid is no better than switching it off on the same number of untimed decisions, so a gate here would buy a shorter holding period, not a signal. The closest arm is the vol gate: +0.86pp of drawdown against the frozen 1.0pp bar, and it does beat its own placebo by +5.00pp -- which is why it is named as the re-test candidate on new data, not re-thresholded here. Verdict NO_GATE.

sleeve_paths.sentence: Across 15 decision grids the vol gate beats its own placebo on 15 of them (drawdown edge 0.63..5.00 pp), clears the frozen 1.0 pp drawdown bar on 6, and keeps 0.95 of baseline CAGR on 15 -- the gain ranges 0.50..1.69 pp. Verdict NO_GATE: a real timing effect that still does not clear the frozen drawdown bar on most grids.

verdict.rule: LOOKAHEAD_PRESENT iff the published engine still takes its signal from bar d (`score.loc[d]`) while paying the book from bar d's open to the next bar's open -- a source pin read at run time -- AND pricing the same rule one bar later costs >= tol_pp_per_year; MECHANISM_ABSENT if the engine no longer reads its own bar (the pin flips, the claim must be re-derived); WITHIN_TOL if the pin holds but the one-bar price is under the line
verdict.why: the published engine ranks on `score.loc[d]` -- built from bar d's own close and amount -- and then earns open[d]->open[d+1]: the book buys at a price that was set before the information it ranks on. Delaying that information one bar costs 1.14 pp/yr, and the whole ladder is monotone in delay (-2:+15.98, -1:+12.46, +0:+9.60, +1:+8.46, +5:+7.39, +20:+5.09)

rows.question: can the one-bar price be earned back by a causal rule
is anything visible between the close and the fill worth that price
does slicing the rebalance over k opens buy anything

research_arc.sentence: **Research arc: all three asks were priced and none paid.** E25 IRRECOVERABLE (+0.07pp best arm `smooth_k2`), E26 MIXED_ACROSS_PHASES (+0.81pp best arm `excl_upgap_q80`), E27 NO_SLICING_EDGE (-0.01pp best arm `k5`). So the gap between the printed number and the tradable one is not recoverable by smoothing the score, not visible in the overnight gap, and not saved by slicing the fill over k opens. This is not a claim that no lever exists -- it is the narrower, earned claim that these three do not pay, and that a fourth question has to come from somewhere other than this rule's own mechanics.
